device.name: Genesis Humanoid RL (Unitree G1 walking environment)

facts.text: The environment imports Env and spaces from gymnasium
HumanoidWalkingEnv subclasses gymnasium.Env
reset loads the Unitree G1 from assets/robots/g1/g1_29dof.urdf and spawns it at (0, 0, 1.0)
The action space is Box(low=-1.0, high=1.0, shape=(num_joints,), dtype=np.float32)

The observation space is an unbounded Box of 3 + 4 + 3 * num_joints + 1 values: base position (3), orientation quaternion (4), joint positions, joint velocities, previous action and target velocity (1)
The constructor defaults are simulation_fps=100, control_freq=20, episode_length=1000 and target_velocity=1.0
The scene uses dt=1.0/simulation_fps, 10 substeps and show_viewer=False
Each control step advances simulation_fps // control_freq scene steps
step clips the action to [-1.0, 1.0] and adds action * 0.1 to the current joint positions before position control
An episode is truncated when current_step >= episode_length
The episode terminates when the base height is below 0.3, |x| > 10.0 or |y| > 5.0, or the base height is above 2.0

The reward adds a forward-velocity term capped at 2.0 times target_velocity, a stability term weighted 0.5 and a height term around 0.8 weighted 0.3, and subtracts energy and smoothness penalties capped at 10.0 and 2.0 with weight 0.1
The observation concatenates base position (3), quaternion (4), joint positions, joint velocities, previous action and target velocity (1)
reset returns (observation, {})
reset creates a new Genesis scene and adds the ground plane and the robot on every call
SB3HumanoidEnv constructs a HumanoidWalkingEnv and copies its spaces
SB3HumanoidEnv.reset seeds numpy when a seed is given and then resets the wrapped environment
make_humanoid_env names the environment HumanoidWalk-v0 and validates the wrapper with check_env
The project requires Python >=3.10,<3.11 and depends on genesis-world, stable-baselines3 and gymnasium
The G1 asset README lists the g1_29dof model with 6*2 leg, 3 waist and 7*2 arm joints
The README describes the project as a full 35-DOF humanoid robot simulation

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds Gymnasium's generator (humanoid_env.py:75) and SB3HumanoidEnv.reset seeds numpy (sb3_wrapper.py:62-63), but the reset draws no random initial state: the G1 is spawned, grounded and settled deterministically.  cap.world.seed.v1 supplies the seed of the next reset; the fake repeats a trajectory for every seed and echoes the seed without changing its start state.

gaps: the fake backend is a pure Python kinematic stand-in for HumanoidWalkingEnv: it runs no Genesis scene, integrates no rigid-body contacts, gravity, actuator torque or sensor noise, and was never compared with the upstream simulator

the fake uses 6 stand-in joints; the real environment sizes its action and observation spaces from robot.n_dofs after loading g1_29dof.urdf, so the real arrays are larger (the README describes a 35-DOF humanoid and the asset table lists 29 joint DOF for g1_29dof)
the fake moves each joint by action * 0.1 and keeps the base at the spawn point; upstream drives Genesis position control and lets the base move, fall and terminate
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (50 ms) only; render() is a no-op and no Genesis viewer is modelled
no snapshot and restore: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state
the fake does not model the automatic grounding step: it keeps the spawn height instead of the height RobotGroundingCalculator computes (humanoid_env.py:112-120)
no physical G1 or hardware is modelled and no result was validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
